I am 60 years old and have farmed these 3 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I know this land well. My wife and I manage it together with our well. We grow wheat in winter and maize in summer — that is the only sensible way here on the North China Plain, and every household around us does the same.

For my wheat this year: I will rotary till the field right after the maize harvest in October. I will sow about 30 jin of improved wheat seed per mu. Before sowing, I will spread compound fertilizer as a base — roughly 50 kg per mu. When the wheat greens up in spring, I will topdress with urea at the jointing stage. All together, that comes to about 18 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I have a well, so I will irrigate three times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. I will spray pesticides three times in total — herbicide once after sowing, and insecticide once or twice when aphids or diseases show up. If the weather is normal, I expect around 1000 kg per mu.

For my maize: As soon as I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize seed without tilling. There are barely 100 days before frost, and no-tillage saves time and keeps soil moisture. I will put down compound fertilizer at planting — about 16 kg of nitrogen, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice: once when the tassels come out and once during grain filling. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide once, so two pesticide applications in total. I expect about 1100 kg per mu from the maize.

This plan has worked for me for decades. I might adjust a little depending on seed prices and the spring rains, but the basics never change. My wife and I can handle this ourselves.
